trigger: The caller wants something that touches their account: an invoice, a payment, a balance, a charge they are disputing, or a credit. Run this before discussing any of it, once per call.

steps.instruction: Tell the caller that only a verified contact can be given account information, and that you need to confirm a few details first. One sentence, in your own words, matching how they have been speaking.
Ask for the email address on the account. Take whatever they say, including if they spell it out.
Check the email. Send field 'email' and the value exactly as the caller said it, not corrected or completed.

fallback.instruction: Tell the caller you could not complete the check just now and that nothing has changed on the account. Offer to have a colleague call them back.

steps.instruction: Tell the caller the check could not be completed just now and nothing has changed on the account. Do not say whether any detail they gave was right — you do not know. Offer to have a colleague call them back.

Ask them to spell the address out, letter by letter, including any hyphen or dot. Say you want to be sure you have it down correctly. Do not say it was wrong, and do not suggest a correction of your own -- Swiss names are frequently misheard and the likeliest problem is how you heard it, not what they said.
Check the spelled-out email. Send field 'email' and the spelled value.
Ask for the phone number on the account. Any format they give is fine.
Check the phone number. Send field 'phone' and the digits exactly as the caller said them.
Ask for their date of birth.
Check the date. Send field 'date_of_birth' and the date exactly as the caller said it, with no reordering.

Tell the caller the check could not be completed just now and nothing has changed on the account. Do not say whether any detail they gave was right — you do not know. Offer to have a colleague call them back.

The date could be read two ways. Ask which they meant by naming the month in words for both readings, for example 'the eleventh of June, or the sixth of November?'. Use the two readings the tool returned. This is about how the date was written down, not about whether it is right.
Check the clarified date. Send field 'date_of_birth' in YYYY-MM-DD form using the reading the caller chose.
Send all three details together: email as confirmed, phone, and date of birth. This is the decision -- nothing before it verified anyone.

fallback.instruction: Tell the caller you could not complete the check and nothing has changed on the account. Offer a colleague.

steps.instruction: Tell the caller the check could not be completed just now and nothing has changed on the account. Do not say whether any detail they gave was right — you do not know. Offer to have a colleague call them back.
Thank them briefly and move straight on to what they called about. Do not recap which details were checked.
Tell the caller you cannot continue with the account on this call and a colleague will take over. Never say why, and do not invite them to try again.

fallback.instruction: Tell the caller you were not able to confirm their identity and you will pass them to a colleague. Never say which detail did not match.
